# Official-data frontend fixtures (real payloads)

Captured 2026-10-12 from the real backend routes (unless a row says otherwise), never hand-written:

| File | Source |
|---|---|
| `official_data.en_report.en.json`, `official_data.en_report.zh.json` | `GET /api/report/<id>/official-data?lang=en|zh` (Flask test client) for a real-bundle publication (`backend/tests/fixtures/data_sources/real/report_bundle-2026-10-11.json` published by the report agent). `official_data.series` is trimmed to three carried series (UNRATE, IMF WEO world GDP growth, Treasury debt to the penny) without provenance/notes; `indicators` is complete. |
| `binary_forecasts.en_report.json` | `binary_forecasts` of `GET /api/report/<id>/forecast` for the same publication (nine admitted `data_anchor`s with `empirical_base_rate`). |
| `viz_manifest_official.en_report.json`, `viz_manifest_official.zh_report.json` | Official-data items of `GET /api/report/<id>/viz-manifest` for the English publication and a Chinese one (`source_caption` harmonized to the report's own `[S#]`). |
| `datasets_manifest.v3_run.json` | `GET /api/research/<pid>/artifact/datasets` body shape around the real `handoff/data/datasets.json` of a v3 research run (provenance/notes/api_url dropped). |
| `datasets_manifest.usaspending_fy.json` | The `data/datasets.json` that the real data layer writes for `usgov:spending/total` (fiscal-year periods in `provenance.periods`): `DataSources` replayed the real capture `backend/tests/fixtures/data_sources/real/providers/usgov_spending_total_fy.json` at its capture clock, then `write_dataset_files` wrote the manifest (generated 2026-10-13 UTC, unmodified), wrapped in the artifact route's `{success, data: {name, content}}` envelope. |
| `binary_forecast.mts_nsa_pooled.json` | `forecast_extractor._normalize_binaries` output (generated 2026-10-14 under the seasonal-basis contract, unmodified) for the committed real carrier `backend/tests/fixtures/data_sources/real/v3_engine/series-2026-10-11.json` (`usgov:treasury/mts_deficit`, 72 NSA monthly observations to 2026-08) with a `>= 0` anchor for 2027-09 (h = 13) and probability 0.6: August starts give too few 13-step changes for a same-month sample or a seasonal profile, so its `empirical_base_rate` pools the start months (`seasonal_basis: all_start_months`, p 0.2373, n 59), which `_binary_quality` never flags. |
| `binary_forecast.eia_nsa_profile.json` | `forecast_extractor._normalize_binaries` output (generated 2026-10-14 under the seasonal-basis contract, unmodified) for the committed live carrier `backend/tests/fixtures/data_sources/real/agent_usage/carriers-2026-10-13.json` (`q2_datacenter`, EIA US commercial electricity sales, NSA monthly) with the anchor, statement, criteria and probability (0.4) of `test_seasonal_profile_is_disclosed_wherever_the_rate_is_shown`: too few July starts for a same-month sample, so the sample is the July seasonal mean plus the pooled deviations (`seasonal_basis: seasonal_profile`, p 0, n 112), which `_binary_quality` still flags (+40 pp). |
| `official_data.usaspending_fy.en.json`, `binary_forecasts.usaspending_fy.json` | Generated 2026-10-14 by the current backend, unmodified: the real USAspending capture `backend/tests/fixtures/data_sources/real/providers/usgov_spending_total_fy.json` replayed through `DataSources` at its capture clock gives the carrier row of `usgov:spending/total` (annual US federal fiscal years, `provenance.periods` to FY2027); the first file is the `GET /official-data` `data` shape built with the route's own `report_agent.official_indicator_rows` (lang en, tag S1); the second holds two `_normalize_binaries` anchors on it, 2026-10-01 (stored, read FY2027 by `forecast_extractor.official_anchor_period_text`) and 2027-10-01 (not stored yet, FY2028). |
| `data_sources_probe.live.json` | Live `probe_data_sources()` output (six MCP servers; key names and states only). |
| `data_sources_probe.endpoint.json` | Live `POST /api/settings/data-sources/test` body through the Flask route (key names and states only; the capture asserted no key value appears). |
